CALCULATOR.SECTION_DESCRIPTION: This section explains which parameters affect the final price, lead time and the final outcome, and how to read the result correctly.

overview.TITLE: What the calculator returns
overview.DESCRIPTION: The calculator returns the final print price, print time and material consumption.
overview.DETAIL: you can choose both material and color.

basic.TITLE: Basic mode
basic.DESCRIPTION: In Basic you choose material, color and quality.
basic.DETAIL: Draft = 0.28 mm, 15% grid. Standard = 0.20 mm, 15% grid. High Definition = 0.12 mm, 20% gyroid.
basic.NOTE: you do not need to manage each print parameter in detail.

advanced.TITLE: Advanced mode
advanced.DESCRIPTION: In Advanced you directly control material, color, nozzle, layer height, infill, pattern and supports.
advanced.DETAIL: Available combinations depend on the active machine profiles.
advanced.NOTE: you already know the exact settings you want to apply to your file.

PARAMETERS.TITLE: Calculator parameters
PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Below you can find the controls currently available in the calculator. In Advanced mode, these are the parameters that affect the final price, lead time and the final finish.

material.TITLE: Material
material.EXPLANATION: The material can be chosen from the active variants currently available, each one linked to the colors that can be ordered.
material.CALCULATOR_EFFECT: It affects material price and the options available in the calculator.

quality.TITLE: Quality
quality.EXPLANATION: In Basic you do not set layer height and infill separately: you choose a predefined preset.
quality.CALCULATOR_EFFECT: It automatically defines layer height, infill pattern and density.

nozzleDiameter.TITLE: Nozzle diameter
nozzleDiameter.EXPLANATION: The calculator currently offers 0.40 mm and 0.60 mm nozzles. Each nozzle unlocks different layer heights and may involve changeover costs.
nozzleDiameter.CALCULATOR_EFFECT: It affects which layer heights can be selected and may influence setup cost.

layerHeight.TITLE: Layer height
layerHeight.EXPLANATION: The available layer heights depend on the selected nozzle.
layerHeight.CALCULATOR_EFFECT: It directly affects print time and part definition.

infill.TITLE: Infill
infill.EXPLANATION: The infill percentage is set manually to match the desired balance of strength, weight and lead time.
infill.CALCULATOR_EFFECT: It increases or reduces weight and time depending on the chosen density.

infillPattern.TITLE: Infill pattern
infillPattern.EXPLANATION: Patterns such as grid, gyroid and cubic are available.
infillPattern.CALCULATOR_EFFECT: It affects the internal structure of the part and can change time, material use and mechanical behavior.

supports.TITLE: Supports
supports.EXPLANATION: You can enable or disable them directly according to the geometry of the file.
supports.CALCULATOR_EFFECT: It changes the print path and can increase both time and material.

GUIDES.TITLE: Practical examples for reading layer height, nozzles and infill
GUIDES.DESCRIPTION: These examples help explain how layer height, nozzles and infill affect the result. In the calculator, the available nozzles are 0.40 mm and 0.60 mm, and each one unlocks different layer heights.

layer-012.TITLE: Layer 0.12 mm
layer-012.OBJECT_EXAMPLE: Miniature or small text with fine detail.
layer-012.CALCULATOR_READ: More visible detail, but longer print times.

layer-020.TITLE: Layer 0.20 mm
layer-020.OBJECT_EXAMPLE: Standard functional part or technical cover.
layer-020.CALCULATOR_READ: Balanced setup, suitable for a standard use case.

layer-028.TITLE: Layer 0.28 mm
layer-028.BEST_FOR: Lower lead time and larger parts.
layer-028.CALCULATOR_READ: Faster print, with a rougher finish.

nozzles-040-060.TITLE: Nozzles 0.40 mm and 0.60 mm
nozzles-040-060.OBJECT_EXAMPLE: 0.40 mm for general use, 0.60 mm for faster or stronger parts.
nozzles-040-060.BEST_FOR: Choosing the right balance between detail and productivity.
nozzles-040-060.CALCULATOR_READ: In the calculator, 0.40 mm opens finer layers; 0.60 mm favors taller layers and faster printing.

infill-15.TITLE: Infill 15% + 2 walls
infill-15.CALCULATOR_READ: Uses less material and usually keeps print time lower.

infill-40.TITLE: Infill 40% + 4 walls
infill-40.TRADEOFF: Higher weight and longer print time.
infill-40.CALCULATOR_READ: Increases material and print time, moving closer to a more solid part.

SOURCES.TITLE: Sources consulted
SOURCES.DESCRIPTION: Here you can find all the sources used for the technical data and material descriptions.

tpu-95a-hf.NAME: TPU 95A HF
tpu-95a-hf.SUMMARY: Very flexible material, useful when you need to absorb shocks and vibrations.
QUALITY_TIPS: Reduce speed and acceleration for more stable extrusion.
Use medium to tall layers to reduce artifacts on soft surfaces.
PROS: Very high flexibility and impact resilience.
Good layer adhesion on soft geometries.
CONS: Sensitive to moisture during printing and storage.
Very low stiffness and limited heat resistance.

pla-basic.NAME: PLA Basic
pla-basic.SUMMARY: Straightforward choice for quick prototypes with good finish and stable printing behavior.
QUALITY_TIPS: For visual quality use 0.12-0.16 mm layers.
PROS: Very good surface quality on visual parts.
CONS: Poor resistance to heat and prolonged UV exposure.

pla-matte.NAME: PLA Matte
pla-matte.SUMMARY: PLA with a matte finish for presentation models and appearance-first parts.
QUALITY_TIPS: 0.16-0.24 mm layers keep the matte effect more even.
PROS: Prints as easily as standard PLA.
CONS: Limited mechanical properties for structural use.
Heat sensitive like other PLA materials.

pla-tough-plus.NAME: PLA Tough+
pla-tough-plus.SUMMARY: Compromise between easy-to-print PLA and better toughness for light functional use.
QUALITY_TIPS: 0.20 mm layers are a good balance between speed and precision.
Use 3-4 walls to improve impact robustness.

asa.NAME: ASA
asa.SUMMARY: Technical outdoor polymer, more UV stable than ABS.
QUALITY_TIPS: An enclosed chamber and brim reduce warping.
0.20-0.28 mm layers balance adhesion and lead time.
CONS: Can warp without an adequate setup.

pc.NAME: PC
pc.SUMMARY: Technical material with high mechanical and thermal resistance for robust parts.
QUALITY_TIPS: A heated chamber and very dry material are preferred.
0.20-0.28 mm layers reduce residual stress compared with very fine layers.
PROS: Very resistant to impact and heat.
High dimensional stability on technical parts.
CONS: Demanding to print at high temperatures.
An imperfect setup easily leads to deformation.

pa12-cf.NAME: PA12-CF
pa12-cf.SUMMARY: Carbon-reinforced nylon focused on stiffness and stability for functional parts.
QUALITY_TIPS: Material and environment must be dry before printing.
0.20-0.28 mm layers with a hardened nozzle and the recommended setup work best.
PROS: Good dimensional stability for technical fixtures.
CONS: Higher cost and printing complexity than entry-level materials.
Requires moisture control and a suitable nozzle.

petg-extrudr.NAME: PETG
petg-extrudr.SUMMARY: Versatile, durable PETG also used for projects involving limited food contact. The supplier declares the filament suitable, but the finished FDM part is not certified as food safe.
QUALITY_TIPS: Use a heated bed and a clean surface for reliable adhesion.
For food-contact requests, we assess the food, temperature, contact duration and cleaning method in writing.
PROS: Good mechanical strength, layer adhesion and heat resistance up to approximately 90 °C.
Suitable for functional parts and 100% recyclable according to the product page.
CONS: FDM layer lines and micro-gaps make cleaning and disinfection less straightforward.
The printed product is not certified as food safe for continuous or prolonged professional use.
IDEAL_FOR: Brief, occasional contact with cold or room-temperature food, subject to assessment

pet-cf.NAME: PET-CF
pet-cf.SUMMARY: Rigid technical material with carbon fiber, very stable on precision parts.
QUALITY_TIPS: A hardened nozzle is mandatory because of the abrasive fiber.
0.20-0.28 mm layers balance adhesion and final stiffness.
CONS: Abrasive: a hardened nozzle is required.
High cost, not ideal for low-cost prototypes.

FAQ.TITLE: Mini FAQ
FAQ.SUBTITLE: Quick answers to the questions that most often block non-technical users.

FILES.A: You can upload STL or 3MF files. If you download a model from an external portal, make sure it is an actual 3D file and not just images or documentation.

MODE.Q: How do I choose between Basic and Advanced?
MODE.A: Choose Basic if you want a fast quote for a ready file. Choose Advanced if you need to compare materials or change settings that affect time, weight and price.

NO_MODEL.Q: What if I do not have a 3D model yet?
NO_MODEL.A: You can search on the platforms listed above or contact us if you need help with CAD design or adaptation.

PRICE.Q: Is the shown price already reliable?
PRICE.A: It is an automatic estimate based on your file and the selected settings. Advanced mode is more precise because it accounts for more print parameters.

BEFORE_UPLOAD.Q: What should I check before uploading?
BEFORE_UPLOAD.A: Check that the model has the correct scale, that the file is not corrupted and that the geometry really matches the final part you want to print.

META.CONTROLLER: Data controllers: Matteo Caletti and Joe Kung (3D-Fab.ch).

S1.TITLE: 1. What data we process
S1.P1: 1.1. We collect the data required for quotes and orders: first name, last name, email, phone, address, shipping/billing data and order details.
S1.P2: 1.2. When you upload 3D files or technical attachments, files are processed only for analysis, production, support and order management.

S2.TITLE: 2. Purpose of processing
S2.P1: 2.1. We use data exclusively to: prepare quotes, confirm orders, receive payments, organize shipments and provide after-sales support.
S2.P2: 2.2. We do not use data for profiling, automated marketing or sale to third parties.

S3.TITLE: 3. Storage of files and data
S3.P1: 3.1. Files uploaded only for quoting are stored for the session duration and automatically removed when it expires.
S3.P2: 3.2. Files and data linked to confirmed orders are stored for the time necessary for production, delivery, support and administrative/legal obligations, then deleted or minimized.
S3.P3: 3.3. Files uploaded in the calculator are used only for technical analysis and quote estimation and remain associated exclusively with the calculator session.

S4.TITLE: 4. Cookies and tracking
S4.P1: 4.1. We do not use profiling, marketing or third-party tracking cookies.
S4.P2: 4.2. We do not use advertising tracking systems. Any temporary technical data is used only for session operation.
S4.P3: 4.3. Public QR links generated from the back-office may record scan date/time, browser-estimated language and a technical visitor estimate obtained through an irreversible hash. We do not request GPS from the phone and we do not store the IP address in plain text.

S5.TITLE: 5. Data sharing
S5.P1: 5.1. We share data only with suppliers strictly necessary for the service (hosting, payments, shipping), limiting it to essential information.
S5.P2: 5.2. Suppliers process data according to contractual instructions and appropriate security measures.

S6.TITLE: 6. User rights
S6.P1: 6.1. You can request access, rectification, deletion or restriction of processing of your data, within the limits provided by law.
S6.P2: 6.2. For any privacy request write to info@3d-fab.ch. The Italian version of this privacy policy is the only legally binding version, unless otherwise agreed in writing.
